}

# Page 30 data (remaining states)

    'Wisconsin': 117667,

}

# Combine all states
all_states = {**data_page29, **data_page30}

# Verify we have 50 states
print(f"Number of states: {len(all_states)}")

# Values in thousands of dollars (as required by question)
values = list(all_states.values())

# Sort in descending order for Zipf ranking
sorted_values = sorted(values, reverse=True)
print(f"\nTop 10 values (in thousands):")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values[:10], 1):
    print(f"  Rank {i}: {v}")

# Calculate Zipf exponent using OLS on log-log
# Zipf's law: frequency ~ rank^(-alpha)
# log(frequency) = -alpha * log(rank) + constant
# So we regress log(value) on log(rank)

import math
import statistics

# Prepare data for regression: log(rank) vs log(value)
# Exclude zero values (there are none here)
log_ranks = [math.log(r) for r in range(1, len(sorted_values) + 1)]
log_values = [math.log(v) for v in sorted_values]

# Calculate OLS: log(value) = a + b * log(rank)
# Zipf exponent = -b (the slope, with negative sign)
n = len(sorted_values)
mean_log_rank = sum(log_ranks) / n
mean_log_value = sum(log_values) / n

# Slope (b) = sum((log(rank) - mean) * (log(value) - mean)) / sum((log(rank) - mean)^2)
numerator = sum((log_ranks[i] - mean_log_rank) * (log_values[i] - mean_log_value) for i in range(n))
denominator = sum((log_ranks[i] - mean_log_rank) ** 2 for i in range(n))
slope = numerator / denominator

# Intercept
intercept = mean_log_value - slope * mean_log_rank

# Zipf exponent is -slope
zipf_exponent = -slope

print(f"\nOLS Regression Results:")
print(f"  Slope: {slope:.6f}")
print(f"  Intercept: {intercept:.6f}")
print(f"  Zipf exponent (alpha): {zipf_exponent:.6f}")
print(f"  R²: {1 - sum((log_values[i] - (intercept + slope * log_ranks[i]))**2 for i in range(n)) / sum((log_values[i] - mean_log_value)**2 for i in range(n)):.6f}")

# Round to nearest thousandth
zipf_rounded = round(zipf_exponent, 3)
print(f"\nZipf exponent (rounded to nearest thousandth): {zipf_rounded}")
